title: The High Passage
premise: Oscar Fairweather, a woman railroad engineer who has spent three years surveying closed mountain lines to bury her grief, inherits a dying prospector's map of the High Passage — an abandoned route to the river's forbidden source, where a mining company has been hiding evidence of a catastrophic dam failure that killed a valley town. Pursued by the company's fixers and shadowed by Elias Vane, the government inspector ordered to bury the same truth, she must run the dead line upstream before the dry season ends and the river drops too low to float the evidence out. In the source canyon, Oscar finds the prospector's proof — and learns Elias has known all along; choosing love against duty, he testifies with her, burning his career to bring justice outside the law, while Oscar finally measures her life in years again.
about_author: Marguerite Montrose is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent a decade mapping rail corridors through the northern ranges before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who find their way by reading the land instead of the rules.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. On a closed mountain spur, Oscar Fairweather surveys a dead line she helped decommission, measuring her life in track miles to avoid feeling anything since the accident that ended her engagement. A stranger stumbles into camp bleeding. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked open by interruption.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. The dying prospector, Harkness, trades her his map of the High Passage for a promise: carry it to the river's source before dry season ends. He dies at dawn clutching a brass survey tag from a town that officially never flooded. Emotional beat: grief meets obligation.

chapters.title: Men in Clean Boots
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Company men arrive asking after Harkness with suspiciously clean boots and a warrant with no seal. Oscar hides the map in a theodolite case and lies for the first time in her careful life. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Inspector on the 4:10
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Government inspector Elias Vane boards Oscar's supply train, ostensibly investigating sabotage. He recognizes her name from old files — and recognizes something else he doesn't say aloud. Emotional beat: two guarded people circling.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Following the river upstream by canoe, Oscar deciphers Harkness's annotations: depth soundings that match no flood on record. She realizes the 'natural' disaster that killed Bellhaven was engineered. Emotional beat: the past becoming personal.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Lead
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Fixers ambush her camp at night; she escapes down rapids with a graze wound and loses half her supplies. She understands this is no longer investigation but survival. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Lie Well
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Ordered to file a report confirming natural causes, Elias stalls, haunted by his father's death in a similar 'accident.' He requests the High Passage assignment himself. Emotional beat: duty beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: Junction at Deadfall
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. At an abandoned junction town, Oscar meets Mara Quist, an old telegraph operator who knew Harkness and reveals the company bought every witness's silence — except his. Emotional beat: loneliness eased by unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: Caught in the Same Current
chapters.summary: POV both alternating. Elias catches up to Oscar at Deadfall; instead of arresting her, he reads the map over her fire and says nothing. They strike an uneasy truce: he'll escort her as his 'prisoner.' Emotional beat: trust kindling against judgment.

chapters.title: The Dry Season Clock
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. River levels drop faster than expected; the final passage will be impassable in nine days. The company posts rewards and seals the upper trail. Emotional beat: time becoming the true antagonist.

chapters.title: Elias's Report
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias files a false interim report buying them a week, knowing it ends his career if discovered. He tells Oscar about his father. First kiss, immediately regretted and not regretted. Emotional beat: love declared against duty.

chapters.title: Quist's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Mara taps out a decoy message drawing the fixers east, then burns her office and vanishes into the hills. Oscar carries the guilt of using an old woman as bait. Emotional beat: sacrifice and its cost.

chapters.title: Portage of Bones
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. The pair portage through a canyon littered with equipment from the original cover-up crew — including a second brass tag matching Harkness's. Someone else died carrying this truth. Emotional beat: dread deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Chief fixer Rennick corners Elias privately: retire rich, or be named the saboteur. Elias pretends to consider. Emotional beat: temptation weighed and refused.

chapters.title: White Water, Black Night
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Running the last navigable gorge by moonlight to beat the dropping water, they capsize; Oscar saves the waterproof map case and nearly drowns; Elias pulls her out. Emotional beat: mortality faced, love undeniable.

chapters.title: What Harkness Buried
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. At the river's forbidden source they find the sealed survey vault: photographs, core samples, and the company's own memos proving the dam was knowingly underbuilt. Also Harkness's letter naming every silenced witness. Emotional beat: truth made physical.

chapters.title: Rennick at the Source
chapters.summary: POV both. Rennick's men arrive by helicopter; Elias stalls them claiming jurisdiction while Oscar caches copies of the evidence in three places only she can find. Gunfire; Mara reappears with mountain men to even the odds. Emotional beat: allies converging.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. With the river now too low, they descend the dead rail line itself — hand-car on rotted ties, pursued — the route Oscar once measured for grief now carrying her toward justice. Emotional beat: her old life repurposed into courage.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Junction
chapters.summary: POV Elias. At Deadfall, Elias broadcasts the evidence over Mara's restored telegraph wire to every newspaper and federal office at once, then surrenders himself to be arrested for it. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled by breaking rank.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. In a packed inquiry room, Oscar presents the map, the tags, and Harkness's promise kept; witnesses emerge one by one as the evidence surfaces. Rennick's empire cracks. Emotional beat: justice arriving outside the law that failed.

chapters.title: Sentence and Mercy
chapters.summary: POV Elias. Elias accepts censure and loss of commission without appeal; Oscar speaks in his defense, choosing him publicly over the career she could claim from the scandal. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved on both sides.

chapters.title: Measuring Years
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. One year later, Oscar stands at the rebuilt Bellhaven memorial spur as the first train runs; the river runs free, the High Passage is a protected historical route. She and Elias plan a survey of their own — together, unhurried. Emotional beat: peace, and a life measured in years.
